image_alt: Two separated forest-plot panels show nine primary near-eye site-average associations per VLSQ-8 standard deviation. The upper panel shows an absolute hour difference for time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep, with an interval crossing zero. The lower panel shows ratios and percentage changes for eight outcomes; most estimates indicate decreases, but none retained false-discovery-rate-adjusted support.
caption: Figure 1: Primary near-eye site-average associations between VLSQ-8 and nine personal light-exposure metrics. Effects compare scores separated by one participant-level SD. The upper panel is an absolute difference in hours for time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep; the lower panel shows ratios and corresponding percentage changes for eight log-link outcomes. Horizontal bars are 95% Wald CIs; none of the nine associations retained FDR-adjusted support.

image_alt: Two separated forest-plot panels show nine complementary chest site-average associations per VLSQ-8 standard deviation. The upper hour-difference outcome has an interval crossing zero. Most lower-panel ratio estimates are below one, but none retained false-discovery-rate-adjusted support.
caption: Figure 2: Complementary chest site-average associations between VLSQ-8 and nine personal light-exposure metrics. Effects compare scores separated by one participant-level SD. The hour-difference and ratio outcomes remain on separate scales; horizontal bars are 95% Wald CIs. None retained FDR-adjusted support.

image_alt: Equal-axis scatter plot compares eight ratio-scale near-eye estimates on the horizontal axis with chest estimates on the vertical axis. Component 95% confidence intervals, horizontal and vertical null lines, and a dashed identity line are shown. Most estimates lie below zero on the log-ratio scale, but proximity to the diagonal does not establish equivalence.
caption: Figure 3: Near-eye and chest VLSQ-8 associations on identical participant-day samples. The dashed diagonal marks equal point estimates and grey lines mark the null; it is not an equivalence analysis.

image_alt: Multi-panel diagnostic figure for nine primary near-eye models shows residual-versus-fitted patterns and distribution checks. Darkest 10 hour mean has the clearest increase in residual spread, and the sleep-below-1-lux model has a small observed zero mass not reproduced by its Tweedie fit.
caption: Figure 4: Selected primary near-eye model checks for all nine metrics. Panels retain their model-specific transformed or Pearson-residual scales and are diagnostic rather than effect displays.

image_alt: Paired comparison of primary and gap-timing-unaware estimates on identical samples for nine metrics at each placement. Estimates are generally close; all eighteen comparisons are classified as stable within model uncertainty.
caption: Figure 5: Primary and gap-timing-unaware VLSQ-8 associations on identical participant-day samples, shown separately for near-eye and chest placements.
